summary: Browser cache revalidation causes SSE resume atomicity loss and truncates final paragraph
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when resuming a long SSE text generation session from their Chrome browser (service worker + aggressive cache revalidation enabled), the final paragraph of the generated response is often missing or abruptly truncated. The partial payload contains valid JSON up to the truncation point (last sentence cut mid-word).

Impact:
- AtlasDocs' live document editor loses concluding sentences in 13% of resumed sessions for long responses (>1.5k tokens).
- Customer-facing editors show malformed paragraphs; downstream parsers report JSON parse errors when clients try to stitch resumed chunks.

Occurrence:
- Repro rate ~10-15% on customer side; reproduced internally at lower rate (~3%) when browser cache control headers manipulated.

Customer notes:
- Happens after a short connectivity drop (cellular->wifi) or when devtools disables network cache and re-enables it.
- Affected users primarily on Chrome 118-121 on macOS and Win10.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming SSE generation request from AtlasDocs editor using sdk-js (streaming endpoint, chunked choices enabled).
2) During long output (>= 1k tokens), toggle network (simulate offline) or trigger service-worker cache revalidation by toggling devtools 'Disable cache' and reloading the page.
3) Allow client to reconnect and trigger resume logic in sdk-js (client sends resume token and last-offset).
4) Observe final SSE chunks: sometimes the stream ends without terminal 'end' event and final paragraph is truncated in the stitched result.
5) Capture browser network trace and server-side proxy logs for the session ID.
logs: Client-side console excerpt: Error: Unexpected end of JSON input at JSON.parse (<anonymous>) at stitchChunks (sdk.js:324)

Proxy access log (truncated): 2026-03-10T14:22:03Z s-abc123 PROXY_INBOUND: recv 14.2KB; 14.2KB forwarded; 2026-03-10T14:22:04Z s-abc123 PROXY_OUTBOUND: upstream 8.1KB chunk; 2026-03-10T14:22:05Z s-abc123 PROXY_OUTBOUND: upstream connection closed (RST)
Serving runtime debug: KV cache primed; last_token_index=14531; finalization callback invoked; write_stream.close() called
Browser network trace: 206 Partial Content (service-worker fetch-> revalidate 304) followed by subsequent conditional GET returning 200 with Content-Length shorter than expected
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Browser service worker/cache revalidation is returning an older cached segment or trimming content-length causing downstream resume to assume fewer bytes expected; close race between conditional GET and SSE handshake observed.

Hypothesis 2: sdk-js resume logic treats byte-offsets from proxy as authoritative; if upstream connection returns a revalidated 200 with chunked encoding differences, stitcher miscalculates last complete token boundary.
Reproduced internally by toggling 'Disable cache' in Chrome and forcing service worker to revalidate; saw 3% failures matching customer's truncation pattern.

Proxy team observed short window where response headers changed from 'transfer-encoding: chunked' to a cached 'content-length' path during service-worker revalidation; downstream runtime closed stream after finalization but client stitched based on stale offsets.
No evidence of model runtime crashing or 5xx; serving runtime logs show graceful finalization but client never received explicit 'end' control event in some cases.

resolution:
Root cause: race between browser service-worker cache revalidation and proxy resume flow produced inconsistent transfer-encoding/length signals; client-side resume logic used stale byte offsets leading to atomicity loss when stitching resumed SSE chunks.

Workaround: Instruct customers to disable SW caching for streaming endpoints or enable websocket fallback in sdk-js until fix is rolled out.

Fix implemented: Added proxy-side guard to ensure resume responses preserve chunked transfer signals and delay sending finalization until client ack; added token-boundary verification and checksum-based stitching in sdk-js (PRs linked).

Follow-ups:
- Rollout proxy guard to prod-us-east 2026-03-15 (canary first).
- Add automated browser-based e2e test that toggles service-worker cache revalidation to prevent regression.
- Update runbook with 'service-worker caching' troubleshooting steps and include recommended header patterns for streaming endpoints.
notes: This ticket expands resume investigation beyond network-level proxies into browser caching behavior — useful pattern for other streaming truncation investigations.
Consider adding a telemetry flag to SDK to report resume byte mismatch events anonymously (opt-in) so we can detect customer surface area without full logs.
